text: Every part you mould depends on a small ring at the tip of the screw.
Inside the barrel, the turning screw carries plastic forward, and melts it.
Melt builds up in front and pushes the screw back. This is recovery.
The ring slides forward, and melt flows through the gap.
To inject, the screw drives forward like a plunger.
Melt pressure slams the ring back against its seat, and seals it,
so the melt goes forward, into the mould.
What's left in front of the screw is the cushion.
But every shot, the ring and seat wear, faster with glass-filled materials.
A worn ring can't seal. During injection, melt leaks backwards past it.
And the shot size changes from shot to shot.
Warning signs: a cushion that drifts or bottoms out, short shots, and part weights that vary.
So: log the cushion every shift.
Test the ring: hold injection pressure on a full mould, and watch the screw. If it creeps forward, the ring is leaking.
Pull the screw, measure the ring and seat, and replace them as a set.
